# SunkenPanel

<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-component-docs.mjs from ai/component-catalog.json and ai/component-composition.json. Do not edit; run `npm run catalog:sync`. -->

`@kerfjs/ui:sunken-panel` · Kerf UI · component · Structure

A rounded or square-corner lowered application surface with one compact inset and a vertical content stack.

## When to use

Group a vertical list of application content on a visually lowered surface with one owned 8px inset and an explicit rounded or square-corner shape.

- A main content region or nested work area needs a darker/lowered background and one compact inset around a vertical stack.
- Use the default rounded shape for an inset surface; choose square for a flush or edge-to-edge application area.

**Not when:**

- Do not use it merely to add padding, as a substitute for Pane anatomy, or around children that already own the same outer surface.

**Alternatives:**

- [Application layout](./layout.md) (composes-with) — Use layout roles for pane, toolbar, scroll, and ordinary content-stack ownership.

## Imports

- JavaScript: `@kerfjs/ui/sunken-panel` — exports `SunkenPanel`.
- CSS: the browser build of `@kerfjs/ui/sunken-panel` pulls its CSS automatically; import `@kerfjs/ui/sunken-panel.css` manually only without the `browser` export condition.
- Declared side effects: browser-condition-css.

Exact prop names and types: [`@kerfjs/ui/sunken-panel`](../public-api-signatures-v1.md#kerfjsuisunken-panel) in `public-api-signatures-v1.md`. Do not infer props from examples.

## Composition

- Parents: any.
- Contexts: `application-ui`.
- Children: unrestricted.

## State and wiring

**The app owns:** region semantics and accessible name; corner shape; scroll ownership; child ordering and content.

No wiring helper.

## Geometry

Margin: none · border: none · padding: self (layout role: structure). `self` means the component already owns it — do not add wrapper padding, margin, or borders around it.

- The root owns one 8px inset and vertical gap; children own their borders and internal geometry.

## Accessibility

- Pass ariaLabel only when the surface is a distinct named region; otherwise it remains a non-landmark grouping.

## Styling boundary

The component owns its own styles. Configure it through its props and variants; do not override its internals.

Public class hooks (select for layout placement only, never to change the component's look): `kui-sunken-panel`.

Never put `kui-sunken-panel` on an element you write; render `SunkenPanel` instead (`KUI-L103`).

Public tokens it reads: `--kui-sunken-panel-background`, `--kui-sunken-panel-foreground`, `--kui-sunken-panel-gap`, `--kui-sunken-panel-padding`, `--kui-sunken-panel-radius`. Set a token only where its public contract allows; prefer a prop.

Everything else is internal: `kerf-ui-analyze` reports private or unknown `.kui-*` selectors (`KUI-L001`, `KUI-L010`), unknown or private tokens (`KUI-L002`, `KUI-L012`), and any application rule that restyles the component, forced dimensions included (`KUI-L019`).
